summary: A speaker in a crisis says plainly who failed, lists what will be asked of the legislature, and says what will happen if it will not act.
realLife: Roosevelt's first inaugural, March 4, 1933, said it was time to speak frankly, blamed the money-changers and financial leaders, listed the measures he would ask of a special session, and said he would otherwise seek broad emergency powers.
sources: Read the full address and noted the blame, the list of asks and the fallback if Congress does not act.
inGame: The `stand`, `call` and `charge` sections, pulled by blunt and by a world fact such as a bank run or a layoff wave.

turns.what: The speaker blames no one and promises calm.
turns.writesBack: The stand section has no named failure.

turns.what: The speaker lists asks but gives no fallback.
turns.pulledBy: a legislature of the speaker's own party
turns.writesBack: The call section is recorded with no threat.
